answer: The voyage test I would run is NFT held across a bridge since mint: an NFT that crossed once and never came back, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the harbor of that gap is the whole defence in one line. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the ocean of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
